questions.question: Over the last two years at university, our research team _____ on three separate machine learning projects.
questions.explanation: Use the Present Perfect ('has worked') because 'over the last two years' refers to an unfinished time period connecting past experiences to the present.
questions.reference_source: Murphy, R. English Grammar in Use (Unit 14: Present Perfect & Past).

questions.question: Before the new software update was deployed, every single test case _____ by the quality assurance team.
questions.explanation: Passive voice ('was thoroughly examined') is required because the test cases receive the action, which is a standard B1-B2 formal register structure.
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 24: Passive Structures in Formal Writing).

questions.question: If our capstone team _____ the user feedback earlier in the semester, we wouldn't be struggling with major revisions right now.
questions.explanation: This is a mixed conditional: an unreal past condition ('had collected', past perfect) with a present consequence ('wouldn't be struggling'), characteristic of CEFR B2 mastery.
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 84: Mixed Conditionals).

questions.question: The production server crashed right after the demo started. There _____ a sudden spike in network traffic that overwhelmed memory.
questions.explanation: 'Must have been' expresses a logical deduction about a past event with high certainty based on available evidence (CEFR B2 modal deduction).
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 17: Past Modals of Deduction).

questions.question: _____ their primary project milestones ahead of schedule, the interns were asked to assist the cloud infrastructure team.
questions.explanation: The perfect participle clause ('Having accomplished') is used to express an action completed before the main clause action, a key syntactic marker of B2 discourse.
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 58: Participle Clauses with Having Done).

questions.question: Before introducing the new feature, the product team decided to _____ thorough market research among undergraduate students.
questions.explanation: In academic and professional English, the verb 'conduct' collocates naturally with 'research', 'survey', or 'investigation', whereas 'make research' is an unnatural learner error.
questions.reference_source: McCarthy, M. English Collocations in Use: Advanced (Unit 12: Academic Research).

questions.question: When choosing between studying abroad and taking an internship, you should carefully _____ the pros and cons.
questions.explanation: 'Weigh the pros and cons' is the established idiomatic collocation meaning to carefully consider advantages and disadvantages before making a decision.
questions.reference_source: Cambridge English Vocabulary Profile (B2 Idioms: Weighing Options).

questions.question: The introduction of generative AI tools has _____ significant changes in how university students write and evaluate research.
questions.explanation: 'Bring about' is a B2 phrasal verb meaning to cause something to happen or produce a notable transformation.
questions.reference_source: McCarthy & O'Dell. English Phrasal Verbs in Use: Advanced (Unit 22: Change & Cause).

questions.question: While the proposed algorithm is theoretically sound, its high computational complexity makes it hardly _____ for real-time mobile devices.
questions.explanation: 'Feasible' (B2 academic adjective) means possible and practical to do easily or conveniently under realistic constraints.
questions.reference_source: English Vocabulary Profile (B2 Academic Lexis: Feasibility & Viability).

questions.question: To overcome this technical bottleneck, our development team had to think _____ and explore unconventional system architectures.
questions.explanation: 'Think outside the box' is an essential workplace and academic idiom meaning to think creatively from a fresh, unconventional perspective.
questions.reference_source: Downes, C. Cambridge English for Job-hunting (Unit 4: Problem Solving & Innovation).

questions.question: _____ the technical team encountered several unexpected server failures, they managed to deliver the prototype on schedule.
questions.explanation: 'Although' correctly introduces a subordinate finite clause with a subject ('the technical team') and verb ('encountered'). 'In spite of' requires a noun phrase or gerund.
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 81: Concession & Contrast Connectors).

questions.question: The survey results clearly show high student enthusiasm. _____, financial constraints will prevent the department from purchasing new lab servers this year.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' is a formal B2 adversative discourse adverb used to signal a contrast with what has just been stated.
questions.reference_source: Council of Europe (2020). CEFR Companion Volume (Coherence and Cohesion B2 Descriptors).

questions.question: Traditional lectures primarily focus on passive listening, _____ interactive workshops encourage collaborative problem-solving.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' is used to highlight a direct comparison or contrast between two facts or ideas in two balanced clauses (characteristic B2 marker).
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 82: Comparative Connectors).

questions.question: The database connection was inadvertently left unindexed; _____, the query execution time multiplied by ten during peak hours.
questions.explanation: 'Consequently' is a formal transition adverb introducing an inevitable result or logical consequence of the previous statement.
questions.reference_source: Council of Europe (2020). CEFR Companion Volume: Discourse Structuring & Propositional Logic.

questions.question: _____ the implementation costs are notably high, the long-term energy savings make the renewable campus initiative worthwhile.
questions.explanation: 'Even though' connects a concession clause to a main clause with emphasis on reality (unlike 'however', which cannot subordinate a clause directly).
questions.reference_source: Murphy, R. English Grammar in Use (Unit 113: Although, Even though, In spite of).

questions.question: Dalam rapat kerja, rekanmu mengusulkan solusi yang menurutmu melebihi anggaran. Kalimat manakah yang paling mencerminkan kesantunan dan profesionalisme tingkat B2 (tactful disagreement)?

options.A: I disagree with you because your calculation is totally wrong.
options.B: I see your point, but we might want to evaluate the budget implications before finalizing this.
options.C: No, I think my idea is much better for our team.
options.D: That proposal is too expensive, let's stop talking about it.

questions.explanation: B2 pragmatic competence requires diplomatic hedging ('I see your point, but we might want to...') rather than abrupt personal dismissal, maintaining collaboration while critically evaluating constraints.
questions.reference_source: Downes, C. Cambridge English for Job-hunting (Unit 6: Managing Disagreements Tactfully).

questions.question: Ketika pewawancara kerja menanyakan: 'Tell me about a time you resolved a conflict within your team', pembuka manakah yang menerapkan kerangka STAR (Situation/Task) secara terstruktur?

options.A: I always get along with everyone because I am a very friendly person.
options.B: During our final semester capstone project, our team had conflicting views on the database architecture, so I organized an evaluation session to compare options.
options.C: Conflict is bad, but my friend made a mistake and I fixed it for him.
options.D: I don't really remember any conflict, everything was always smooth.

questions.explanation: Effective professional communication requires establishing context (Situation), identifying the challenge (Task), and outlining proactive steps (Action), which is the foundation of the STAR method at B2.
questions.reference_source: Downes, C. Cambridge English for Job-hunting (Unit 5: Behavioral Interview Responses).

questions.question: Dalam seminar skripsi, kamu ingin meminta pembicara menjelaskan metodologi pengujian datanya tanpa terdengar meremehkan. Ungkapan yang paling tepat adalah:

options.A: Explain your data again, it is very confusing.
options.B: Could you elaborate on how you validated your training data sample? I would appreciate more context on that.
options.C: I don't understand anything about your research methodology.
options.D: Why did you use that method? It seems weird.

questions.explanation: 'Could you elaborate on... I would appreciate more context' combines indirect questioning and polite hedging, standard in scholarly B2 academic discourse.
questions.reference_source: Council of Europe (2020). CEFR Sociolinguistic Appropriateness & Academic Politeness.

questions.question: Kalimat manakah yang menunjukkan penggunaan 'academic hedging' (menyampaikan klaim ilmiah secara hati-hati, objektif, dan proporsional sesuai bukti)?

options.A: The experiment definitely proves that all existing solutions are useless.
options.B: The experimental results suggest that this approach may improve speaking fluency under certain conditions.
options.C: My algorithm is 100% the best in the entire field.
options.D: Everyone knows that AI will replace human teachers tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Academic hedging uses tentative verbs ('suggest') and modal qualification ('may improve ... under certain conditions') to make defensible, scientifically honest claims.
questions.reference_source: Hewings, M. Advanced Grammar in Use (Unit 95: Hedging in Scholarly Writing).

questions.question: Di akhir presentasi proyek akhir, ungkapan manakah yang paling ringkas dan profesional untuk merangkum rekomendasi utama tim?

options.A: That's all from me, thank you.
options.B: To sum up, investing in automated unit testing will not only reduce future bugs but also significantly enhance developer velocity.
options.C: I am finished talking now, any questions?
options.D: Finally, I hope you like my presentation.

questions.explanation: Using a formal conclusion marker ('To sum up') combined with correlative structure ('not only ... but also') produces an articulate, persuasive B2 summary.
questions.reference_source: Downes, C. Cambridge English for Job-hunting (Unit 7: Concluding Professional Presentations).
